row.Finding description: Deleting residues 1–71 produced a more complicated and aggregated sedimentation distribution for recombinant apoE4-(72–299) than for apoE3-(72–299) in PBS.
row.Finding quote: Compared with the simplicity in size distribution of apoE3-(72–299), apoE4-(72–299) existed in a more complicated and aggregated pattern (Fig. 1C).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72–299) -> apoE4-(72–299)) -> (greater apoE self-aggregation in PBS)
row.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299), expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3), with C-terminal tags; 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation velocity at 20 °C and 42,000 rpm for 3.5 h; continuous c(s) analysis. Cell-free, non-acidic system.

set.Finding description: In PBS, apoE4-(72–299) had a broader sedimentation distribution than apoE3-(72–299). The species at 8.9 S accounted for 17% of apoE4 versus 3% of apoE3.
set.Finding summary: ApoE4-(72–299) showed a broader distribution and a higher fraction at 8.9 S than apoE3-(72–299) in PBS.

proposal.reason: The Results quote describes this paper’s experiment at 0.5 mg/ml. Both isoforms have a printed value at exactly 8.9 S, so 17/3 quantifies a matched component of the broader distribution. The comparison is between isoforms carrying the same deletion.
proposal.evidence: Results, p. 13335, lists “8.9 (3%)” for apoE3-(72–299) and “8.9 (17%)” for apoE4-(72–299). In the original PDF, Fig. 1C shows additional higher-S peaks in the blue apoE4 trace. The three supplied PNGs all show Fig. 2 and Table 1.

directness.why: Sedimentation of purified apoE fragments at pH 7.3 matches the neutral-pH aggregation reference rows and gives no endo-lysosomal localization.

row.Finding description: Global discrete-species fitting resolved a broader, larger aggregate population for apoE4-(72–299), including a largest fitted species of 666 kDa versus 351 kDa for apoE3-(72–299).
row.Finding quote: ApoE3-(72–299) main- tained a major species of tetramer (by SV) or hexamer (by SE), and apoE4-(72–299) showed a complicated distribution of tetramer (or tri- mer), octamer, decamer, 14-mer, and large aggregates.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72–299) -> apoE4-(72–299)) -> (broader apoE oligomer distribution containing larger aggregates)
row.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299) in aqueous PBS, pH 7.3; global analysis of sedimentation-equilibrium and sedimentation-velocity data at 20 °C; four discrete species fitted for apoE3-(72–299) and six for apoE4-(72–299).

set.Finding description: The global fit resolved six species for apoE4-(72–299) and four for apoE3-(72–299) in PBS. The largest fitted species had masses of 666 and 351 kDa, respectively.

proposal.reason: The Results quote supports the broader distribution. Table 2 quantifies the mass of the largest fitted species, giving 666/351. This ratio describes species size.
proposal.evidence: Table 2, apoE-(72–299), lists apoE3 masses of 23, 94, 165, and 351 kDa and apoE4 masses of 25, 86, 212, 263, 379, and 666 kDa.

directness.why: The discrete-species fit measures purified-fragment oligomerization in neutral PBS, matching the cell-free aggregation references.

row.Finding description: A single-species sedimentation-equilibrium fit gave apoE4-(72–299) a higher equivalent molar mass than apoE3-(72–299) in PBS, 209 versus 192 kDa.
row.Finding quote: The apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299) proteins exhibited a Meq of 192 and 209 kDa, respectively.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72–299) -> apoE4-(72–299)) -> (higher equivalent molar mass in PBS)
row.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299), expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3); 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3; sedimentation equilibrium at 20 °C, four speeds from 6,000 to 20,000 rpm, each for 14 h; single-species SEDPHAT fit to heterogeneous protein populations.
row.Data location: Table 1, ApoE3-(72–299) and ApoE4-(72–299) rows, Mass in PBS column

proposal.reason: The Results quote and Table 1 agree. The apoE4/apoE3 equivalent-mass ratio in PBS is 209/192.
proposal.evidence: Table 1, apoE-(72–299), Mass in PBS: apoE3 192 kDa and apoE4 209 kDa. The Results on p. 13337 print the same pair.

directness.why: Equivalent mass from sedimentation equilibrium of purified apoE in neutral PBS is a surrogate for endo-lysosomal aggregation.

row.Finding description: With 50 mM DHPC, apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299) had monomer-like equivalent molar masses of 30 and 26 kDa, respectively, with no significant difference in oligomeric state reported or statistically tested.
row.Finding quote: In the presence of DHPC, all kinds of apoE proteins maintained a Meq corresponding to their monomer molar mass (Table 1).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72–299) -> apoE4-(72–299)) -> (no change in monomeric apoE state with DHPC)
row.Experimental system: Purified recombinant human apoE3-(72–299) and apoE4-(72–299); 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3, containing 50 mM DHPC; sedimentation equilibrium at 20 °C, four speeds from 6,000 to 20,000 rpm, each for 14 h; single-species SEDPHAT fit; theoretical monomer mass 27 kDa.
row.Data location: Table 1, ApoE3-(72–299) and ApoE4-(72–299) rows, Mass in PBS containing 50 mM DHPC column

set.Finding description: In 50 mM DHPC, the equivalent molar mass of apoE4-(72–299) was 26 kDa versus 30 kDa for apoE3-(72–299). Both were close to the theoretical monomer mass of 27 kDa.
set.Finding summary: Both apoE-(72–299) isoforms had monomer-like masses in DHPC, with a lower fitted mass for apoE4.

proposal.reason: The quote supports the monomer assignment and Table 1 gives the construct-specific equivalent-mass ratio, 26/30. The paper supplies no between-isoform significance test.
proposal.evidence: Table 1, apoE-(72–299): theoretical monomer mass 27 kDa for each. In the 50 mM DHPC column, apoE3 is 30 kDa and apoE4 is 26 kDa.

directness.why: Monomer-like equivalent mass in neutral DHPC-containing buffer measures purified apoE assembly outside an endo-lysosome.

row.Finding description: With 50 mM DHPC, full-length apoE3 and apoE4 became predominantly monomeric, with major low-sedimentation species comprising 79% and 73%, respectively; no significant difference in isoform-specific aggregation was reported or statistically tested.
row.Finding quote: Each protein appeared as a major species at s  1.6–2.2 (79, 73, 65, 75, 85, and 64% for apoE3, apoE4, apoE3-(72–299), apoE4- (72–299), apoE3-(1–231), and apoE4-(1–231), respectively
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in predominantly monomeric apoE state with DHPC)
row.Experimental system: Purified recombinant full-length human apoE3 and apoE4 expressed in E. coli; 0.5 mg/ml in PBS, pH 7.3, containing 50 mM DHPC; sedimentation velocity at 20 °C and 42,000 rpm for 6 h; continuous c(s) analysis. The major species sedimented at 1.6–2.2 S across tested constructs.

set.Finding description: In 50 mM DHPC, both full-length isoforms were predominantly monomeric. The major low-sedimentation species accounted for 73% of apoE4 versus 79% of apoE3.
set.Finding quote: Each protein appeared as a major species at s = 1.6–2.2 (79, 73, 65, 75, 85, and 64% for apoE3, apoE4, apoE3-(72–299), apoE4-(72–299), apoE3-(1–231), and apoE4-(1–231), respectively).
set.Finding summary: Both full-length isoforms were predominantly monomeric in DHPC, with a lower major-species fraction for apoE4.
set.Data location: Fig. 2A and the accompanying Results on p. 13337, Dissociation of ApoE Proteins in the Presence of Dihexanoylphosphatidylcholine Micelles

proposal.reason: The first two printed percentages give the full-length apoE4/apoE3 ratio, 73/79. The two isoforms share a predominant state despite the difference in fractions. The legend’s p = 0.95 is a fitting parameter.
proposal.evidence: Fig. 2A shows dominant low-S peaks for full-length apoE3 and apoE4. The Results assign 79% to apoE3 and 73% to apoE4. No independent replicate count or comparison P value is reported.

directness.why: The major-species fraction measures full-length apoE assembly in neutral DHPC-containing buffer outside an endo-lysosome.

row.Finding description: Surface-biotinylated sortilin internalized in CHO-S cells exposed to apoE3 or apoE4. During recycling, dynasore blocked receptor re-entry. Recycling with apoE4 was 49.56 ± 16.92% versus 100 ± 13.84% with apoE3, normalized to the apoE3 mean (n = 9 biological replicates from three independent experiments).
row.Finding quote: In these studies, the amount of receptors recycling back to the cell surface was reduced by 50% in apoE4-treated as com- pared to apoE3-treated cells (Figures 6D, E
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (reduced recycling of internalized sortilin to the cell surface)
row.Experimental system: CHO cells stably expressing murine sortilin (CHO-S); 5 µg/mL apoE3 or apoE4; surface biotinylation at 4 °C, 15 min internalization at 37 °C, GSH strip, then 60 min recycling with dynasore and GSH strip; streptavidin pulldown and western blot densitometry

set.Finding quote: In these studies, the amount of receptors recycling back to the cell surface was reduced by 50% in apoE4-treated as compared to apoE3-treated cells (Figures 6D, E).

proposal.reason: Section 3.5 reports the 50% reduction, and the legend confirms the group means and n = 9. The P threshold comes from the star over the two groups in Fig 6E and the legend key. The direct assay takes strength 1.
proposal.evidence: Fig 6E shows one star above a bracket joining apoE3 and apoE4. The legend gives *P < .05 and reports 49.56 ± 16.92% with apoE4 versus 100 ± 13.84% with apoE3, mean ± SEM, from nine biological replicates across three independent experiments. [Fig 6D–E](https://edoc.mdc-berlin.de/id/eprint/18922/1/18922oa.pdf#page=9)

directness.why: The assay varies apoE isoform and directly measures how much internalized sortilin returns to the cell surface.

row.Finding description: Internalization of surface sortilin into CHO-S cells did not differ between apoE3 and apoE4 treatment (no significant difference); only the recycling step was affected.
row.Finding quote: The detrimental effect of apoE4 was specific for the recycling step of the sorting path as the extent of internalization of sortilin (Figure S5B) or its ligand apoE (Fig- ures S5C, D) was not different comparing apoE3 and apoE4 treatment conditions
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in sortilin internalization)
row.Experimental system: CHO-S cells (murine sortilin) treated with apoE3 or apoE4; sortilin internalization assay (details in supplement)

set.Finding description: After 15 minutes, CHO-S cells exposed to apoE4 had a numerically lower mean amount of internalized biotinylated sortilin than cells exposed to apoE3. The authors report no significant difference.
set.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no significant difference in sortilin internalization at 15 minutes)

proposal.reason: The main text reports the nonsignificant comparison. Supplementary Fig S5B provides a readable mean and its legend gives the replicate count. Neither supplies a numerical P value.
proposal.evidence: In S5B, the axis runs from 0 to 200% of the apoE3 condition. The apoE3 mean is set to 100% and the apoE4 mean line is near 85%. The S5B legend specifies nine biological replicates from three independent experiments and a Student’s t test. [S5B plot](https://edoc.mdc-berlin.de/id/eprint/18922/2/18922suppl.pdf#page=14) [S5B legend](https://edoc.mdc-berlin.de/id/eprint/18922/2/18922suppl.pdf#page=9)

directness.why: The assay directly compares internalization of surface-labeled receptor under apoE3 and apoE4, matching the H2 internalization reference rows.

row.Finding description: Cultured cells expressing APOE4 showed APOE accumulation in enlarged lysosomes and late endosomes relative to the APOE3 condition summarized in Figure 1.
row.Finding quote: Consistent with previous studies showing that expression of APOE4 damages lysosomal membrane integrity, dysregulates endo/lysosomal pH, and results in enlarged endosomes in various models, we found that APOE4 accumulates in enlarged lysosomes and late endosomes (Figure 1).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (APOE accumulation in enlarged lysosomes and late endosomes)
row.Experimental system: Cultured cells studied using fluorescently tagged human APOE3 and APOE4 cell lines. Cell species, cell type/source, age, experimental duration, and measurement details are not specified. Human brain-cell identity and lipid-mediated causation are not established.
row.Data location: Fig 1; main-text paragraph beginning “Late-onset AD is the most common form of dementia”

set.Finding quote: we found that APOE4 accumulates in enlarged lysosomes and late endosomes (Figure 1).

proposal.reason: The full quote is verbatim. The shortened excerpt isolates the authors’ localization finding from the preceding claims about membrane integrity and pH attributed to prior studies. Figure 1 identifies the APOE3 comparator. P16 gives no numerical effect, P value, or sample size.
proposal.evidence: The first body paragraph states “we found that APOE4 accumulates in enlarged lysosomes and late endosomes (Figure 1).” The Figure 1 legend identifies the comparison as “APOE4 (below, orange) vs. APOE3 (above, blue).”

directness.why: The endpoint is apoE cargo localization in late endosomes and lysosomes, matching the H5 apoE localization reference rows scored 3/4.

row.Finding description: The dimer-to-monomer dissociation rate constant (k-1) was 6.4x10^-4 s-1 for apoE4 versus 5.4x10^-4 s-1 for apoE3; apoE4 dimers dissociate fastest, and the authors say this is the rate-limiting step for lipidation.
row.Finding quote: Table 1 shows that the rate constants for dissociation of dimers to monomers (k-1) are different for the isoforms, being fastest for apoE4 and slowest for apoE2.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (faster dimer-to-monomer dissociation, k-1)
row.Experimental system: Recombinant full-length human apoE4 vs apoE3, pH 7.4 HEPES buffer, 25 C, with DMPC SUVs (0.25 mg/mL); kinetic modeling with KinTek Explorer

set.Finding description: In fits to DMPC vesicle-clearance data, the dimer-to-monomer dissociation rate constant k−1 was 6.4×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ for WT apoE4 versus 5.4×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ for WT apoE3. The authors identified dimer dissociation as rate-limiting for lipidation at apoE concentrations near or above 100 nM.

proposal.reason: The quote is verbatim and describes P33’s own analysis. The authors adjusted k−1 when fitting the clearance data. Table 1 supports the direction and the 1.19x ratio (6.4/5.4), with printed_in_text provenance. No comparison-specific P value or sample size is reported. The description needs the concentration qualifier, and the readout warrants class 3.
proposal.evidence: Table 1, k−1 column, lists “6.4×10-4” for WT-apoE4 and “5.4×10-4” for WT-apoE3. The Discussion states that “the dissociation of the dimers to the monomers is the rate determining step at concentrations near or above 100 nM apoE.”

directness.why: The fitted rate of apoE dimer dissociation in a cell-free assay at pH 7.4 is a surrogate for endo-lysosomal apoE aggregation.

row.Finding description: For peptide 230–243, the model assigned 7 ± 1 wild-type ApoE3 amides and 8 ± 1 wild-type ApoE4 amides to the slow bin. Both monomeric mutants had 10 ± 1 in the fast bin. These counts support the authors’ qualitative conclusion of similar oligomerization properties. The paper reports no test of isoform equivalence.
row.Finding summary: Wild-type ApoE3 and ApoE4 showed similar slow-bin counts for peptide 230–243.
row.Experimental system: Recombinant human wild-type and monomeric-mutant (F257A/W264R/L279Q/V287E) ApoE3 and ApoE4; H/DX at pH 7.4, 25 °C, 0.5-60 min after dilution 4 µM to 400 nM; fixed-rate-constant binning fit (MathCAD)

proposal.reason: The quote accurately reproduces Table 1. For peptide 230–243, the model assigned one more amide to the slow bin for wild-type ApoE4 than for wild-type ApoE3 (8 − 7). This is a descriptive difference in fitted amide counts. Both monomeric mutants had 10 ± 1 amides in the fast bin. The paper gives no P value for the isoform comparison and reports only a lower bound of three replicates, so the exact sample size remains N/A.
proposal.evidence: Table 1, peptide 230–243, wild-type rows in column order 10, 1, 0.1 min⁻¹: “ApoE3 | 0 ± 0 | 3 ± 1 | 7 ± 1” and “ApoE4 | 1 ± 0 | 1 ± 0 | 8 ± 1”. Methods: “All experiments were performed in at least triplicate.” Authors’ interpretation: “We found that the three wild-type isoforms largely share oligomerization properties.”

directness.why: Peptide-level H/D exchange measures protection at a self-association interface in purified ApoE at pH 7.4, a weak surrogate for endo-lysosomal ApoE aggregation consistent with the H3 solvent-accessibility reference row.

row.Finding description: In PBS, apoE4-(72-166) formed a smaller intermediate oligomer than apoE3-(72-166), 51 versus 68 kDa, interpreted as tetramer versus hexamer, but its fitted local concentrations were higher: 0.18 versus 0.16 A280 in velocity and 0.05 versus 0.04 A280 in equilibrium.
row.Finding quote: In the aqueous PBS solution, apoE-(72-166) peptides showed a major species of dimer, tetramer (for apoE4-(72-166)) or hexamer (for apoE2- and apoE3-(72-166)), and large aggregates, respectively, which indicated a significant polymerization.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (lower intermediate-oligomer mass but higher fitted intermediate-species signals in PBS)
row.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, at 20°C; combined sedimentation velocity and multi-speed sedimentation equilibrium fitted with a three-discrete-species model.

proposal.reason: The original quote is verbatim and supports the tetramer and hexamer assignments. The table row also supports the numerical claims. The effect is the apoE4/apoE3 fitted mass ratio, 51/68. The fitted velocity and equilibrium signals are higher for apoE4 by 0.02 and 0.01 A280, respectively.
proposal.evidence: Table 2, PBS, second species, apoE3 then apoE4: “4.8 | 68 | 0.16, 0.04 | 4.7 | 51 | 0.18, 0.05”.

directness.why: The fitted oligomer masses measure apoE fragment self-association in neutral PBS, a surrogate for endo-lysosomal aggregation.

row.Finding description: In 5 mM DHPC, apoE4-(72-166) had higher fitted large-aggregate signals than apoE3-(72-166), 0.04 versus 0.03 A280 in velocity and 0.19 versus 0.06 A280 in equilibrium, while fitted aggregate masses were 217 versus 232 kDa.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (higher fitted large-aggregate signals but lower aggregate mass in 5 mM DHPC)
row.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, with 5 mM DHPC at 20°C; global three-discrete-species sedimentation velocity/equilibrium analysis.

proposal.reason: The effect is the apoE4/apoE3 fitted velocity signal ratio, 0.04/0.03. The equilibrium signal ratio is 0.19/0.06, or 3.17x. The fitted mass is 15 kDa lower for apoE4. All three comparisons match the quoted row.
proposal.evidence: Table 2, 5 mM DHPC, third species, apoE3 then apoE4: “8.4 | 232 | 0.03, 0.06 | 8.5 | 217 | 0.04, 0.19”.

directness.why: The fitted large-aggregate signal measures cell-free apoE fragment assembly at neutral pH in submicellar DHPC.

row.Finding description: In 5 mM DHPC, the dimer-sized species had lower fitted local concentrations for apoE4-(72-166) than apoE3-(72-166), 0.01 versus 0.08 A280 in velocity and 0 versus 0.08 A280 in equilibrium, with fitted masses of 22 versus 21 kDa.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (lower fitted dimer-sized-species signals in 5 mM DHPC)
row.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, with 5 mM submicellar DHPC at 20°C; global three-discrete-species analysis of sedimentation velocity and equilibrium.

proposal.reason: The effect is the apoE4/apoE3 fitted velocity signal ratio, 0.01/0.08. The equilibrium fit gives zero for apoE4 and 0.08 A280 for apoE3. The reported masses are correct.
proposal.evidence: Table 2, 5 mM DHPC, first species, apoE3 then apoE4: “2.5 | 21 | 0.08, 0.08 | 2.2 | 22 | 0.01, 0”.

directness.why: The dimer-sized signal measures purified apoE fragment oligomerization at neutral pH in submicellar DHPC.

row.Finding description: In 100 mM DHPC, the larger apoE4-(72-166)-lipid species had greater fitted mass than the apoE3 counterpart, 58 versus 50 kDa, and higher local concentrations, 0.01 versus 0 A280 in velocity and 0.11 versus 0.10 A280 in equilibrium.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3-(72-166) -> apoE4-(72-166)) -> (higher fitted larger-complex mass and signals in 100 mM DHPC)
row.Experimental system: Recombinant human apoE3- and apoE4-(72-166) fragments in PBS, pH 7.3, with 100 mM DHPC at 20°C; global two-discrete-species sedimentation velocity/equilibrium analysis; mass includes lipid, so peptide stoichiometry is uncertain.

proposal.reason: The effect is the apoE4/apoE3 fitted complex mass ratio, 58/50. The printed apoE3 velocity value is “.0”. Both velocity and equilibrium signals are 0.01 A280 higher for apoE4.
proposal.evidence: Table 2, 100 mM DHPC, second species, apoE3 then apoE4: “2.3 | 50 | .0, 0.10 | 3.0 | 58 | 0.01, 0.11”.

directness.why: The higher fitted mass includes micellar lipid and leaves the peptide stoichiometry unresolved.

row.Finding description: Lysosomal FITC–dextran/Texas Red–dextran ratios showed no significant difference in lysosomal pH between APOE4 and APOE3 neurons across three plates with two wells per genotype per plate.
row.Finding quote: Our results show that endolysosomal pH is not changed in any of the APOE isoform-expressing cortical neurons (Fig. 3C,D).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in lysosomal pH in human cortical neurons)
row.Experimental system: Human cortical neurons from EBiSC isogenic iPSCs BIONi010-C-2 (APOE ε3/ε3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE ε4/ε4); donor age and AD status were not stated. Cells received pH-sensitive FITC–dextran and pH-insensitive Texas Red–dextran for 24 hours, followed by a 24-hour chase; vesicular fluorescence ratios measured by Operetta imaging.

set.Finding summary: No significant difference in baseline lysosomal pH was detected between APOE4 and APOE3 cortical neurons.

proposal.reason: The quote matches the authors’ result. The estimated effect is the APOE4/APOE3 ratio of the plotted FITC/Texas Red signals. The figure gives no calibrated difference in pH units or numerical P value for this comparison.
proposal.evidence: Fig. 3C shows mean fluorescence ratios of about 1.01 for APOE3 and 1.03 for APOE4, with three points per group. The methods specify three plates with two wells per genotype per plate.

directness.why: The genotype comparison directly measures baseline lysosomal pH, matching the H5 acidification reference rows.

row.Finding description: In situ lysosomal calcium measurements showed no significant difference between APOE4 and APOE3 neurons, despite an upward trend in APOE4, using five biological replicates.
row.Finding quote: Although not significant compared with APOE ε3 and APOE ε2, the trend seen in these data further confirms that lysosomal Ca2+ is indeed elevated in APOE ε4-expressing iPSC neurons (P=0.0116 versus APOE−/−).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in lysosomal calcium content by the in situ assay)
row.Experimental system: Human cortical neurons from EBiSC isogenic iPSCs BIONi010-C-2 (APOE ε3/ε3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE ε4/ε4); donor age and AD status were not stated. In situ endolysosomal calcium estimated from calcium-sensitive OGB (0.5 mg/ml) relative to calcium-insensitive Texas Red–dextran (0.1 mg/ml); five biological replicates and one technical replicate per isoform.

set.Finding summary: The in situ lysosomal calcium signal was numerically higher in APOE4 neurons, with no significant difference detected versus APOE3.

proposal.reason: The quote supports a nonsignificant upward trend. The reported P=0.0116 belongs to APOE4 versus APOE-null, so the APOE4 versus APOE3 numerical P value remains unavailable.
proposal.evidence: Fig. 3B shows mean OGB/Texas Red ratios of about 3.5 for APOE3 and 4.0 for APOE4. The marked comparison spans APOE4 and APOE-null. The legend specifies five biological replicates per isoform.

directness.why: Steady-state luminal calcium content is a surrogate for lysosomal function, consistent with the H5 reference for estimated lysosomal calcium levels.

row.Finding description: Mean FluoZin-3-AM spot intensity showed no significant difference between APOE4 and APOE3 neurons in three biological replicates.
row.Finding quote: Our results show that there were no significant differences in Zn2+ levels between the cortical neurons expressing the different APOE isoforms (Fig. S2A–E).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in zinc-probe mean spot intensity)
row.Experimental system: Human cortical neurons from EBiSC isogenic iPSCs BIONi010-C-2 (APOE ε3/ε3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE ε4/ε4); donor age and AD status were not stated. FluoZin-3-AM loading at 5 µM for 30 minutes at 37°C followed by imaging and mean spot-intensity measurement; three biological replicates with one technical repeat.

set.Finding summary: Mean FluoZin-3 spot intensity was numerically lower in APOE4 neurons, with no significant difference detected versus APOE3.

proposal.reason: The quote is the authors’ result for the zinc assays, and the supplementary legend confirms the specific endpoint in D. The figure-wide star key supplies no numerical P value for this unmarked comparison.
proposal.evidence: Supplementary Fig. S2D shows mean spot intensities of about 1.9×10⁵ RFU/cell for APOE3 and 1.6×10⁵ for APOE4. Panel D has no significance bracket. The S2 legend specifies three biological replicates with one technical repeat.

directness.why: Punctate zinc-probe intensity measures an ionic-content surrogate for endolysosomal function.

row.Finding description: Proteomics found mitochondrial proteins enriched in sarcosyl-insoluble aggregates from APOE4-expressing T98G cells relative to APOE3-expressing cells, indirectly suggesting deficient lysosomal clearance.
row.Finding quote: Consistent with deficient autophagy in apoE4-expressing cells, we find that these mitochondrial proteins are enriched in the apoE4 lysates compared to apoE3 lysates.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher mitochondrial-protein abundance in insoluble aggregates, a surrogate of impaired mitophagic clearance)
row.Experimental system: Human ATCC T98G astroglioma cells stably expressing apoE3 or apoE4; sarcosyl-insoluble aggregate proteins separated by SDS-PAGE, trypsin-digested, analyzed by LC-MS, and identified using MASCOT. Mitochondrial cargo abundance was interpreted as a lysosomal/mitophagy surrogate; flux and lipid metabolism were not measured.

set.Finding description: All four mitochondrial proteins listed in Fig. 2C had higher relative abundance in sarcosyl-insoluble aggregates from apoE4 cells than from apoE3 cells under both fed and starved conditions. Impaired mitophagic clearance was inferred.

proposal.reason: The quote is verbatim and the direction holds for every matched-condition comparison. Keep the overall effect qualitative because Fig. 2C reports separate protein abundances and supplies no pooled effect. No protein-specific P value or n is reported.
proposal.evidence: Calculated from the numbers printed in Fig. 2C (visual_only), fed apoE4/apoE3 ratios were 3.49x for ATP5B (192/55), 4.29x for CS (73/17) and 9x for SDHA (63/7). Starved ratios were 6.76x (277/41), 6.17x (74/12) and 22.2x (111/5), respectively. TOMM5 was 2 versus 0 fed and 5 versus 0 starved, so both fold ratios are undefined.

directness.why: Mitochondrial cargo abundance in a whole-cell insoluble fraction is a loose surrogate for mitophagic clearance because the assay measures neither lysosomal delivery nor degradation.

row.Finding description: In six independent mouse-astrocyte experiments, human E4 showed higher intracellular C+C intermolecular FRET than E3, supporting increased apoE–apoE proximity without establishing aggregate burden or endo-lysosomal localization.
row.Finding quote: When comparing the interactions between corresponding combinations of the apoE termini, intermolecular FRET was higher for E4 and lower for E2, with E3 adopting intermediate FRET levels.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher intracellular C+C intermolecular FRET in mouse astrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Primary immortalized mouse astrocytes genetically null for endogenous apoE, transiently co-transfected with human apoE-RFP and apoE-GFP of the same isoform, E3 or E4, at a 1:1 ratio, 0.48 μg/cm2 each; collected 36 h after transfection, fixed in 2% PFA for 10 min, and analyzed by flow-cytometry FRET. Mouse strain and donor age not specified in supplied text; no endo-lysosomal localization.

proposal.reason: The quote is verbatim from the authors’ Results. Figure 3C supports the stated direction and gives both a readable mean FRET ratio and a significance mark specific to the E3–E4 comparison.
proposal.evidence: In Fig. 3C, the leftmost triplet shows intracellular C+C FRET in astrocytes. The E3 mean is 1.0 and the E4 mean is about 1.9 on the normalized emission-ratio axis. The shorter comparison line spans E3 and E4 and carries three asterisks. The Fig. 3 legend defines “*** ≤ 0.001” and identifies panel C as “intermolecular FRET for astrocyte intracellular apoE ( n = 6 independent experiments).”

A subset of e4 carriers had high insoluble ApoE. Insoluble ApoE was also enriched in dementia cases lacking e4. row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4 under cholesterol loading) -> (no change in somatic LAMP1-positive compartment size)

row.Finding description: APOE44 microglia had lower HEXB protein abundance than APOE33 microglia in proteomics using three wells per genotype; enzyme activity was not measured.
row.Finding quote: These data were in agreement with our scRNAseq results, also indicating that lysosomal and endosomal pathways were being downregulated (i.e., LAMP1, LAMP2, HEXA, HEXB) (Figures 3I-K, S3C, Table S6).

directness.why: Whole-cell HEXB protein abundance is a surrogate for lysosomal function and receives the same score as the matched HEXA measurement.

row.Finding description: In six independent mouse-astrocyte experiments, human E4 showed higher intracellular N+C intermolecular FRET than E3, supporting increased apoE–apoE proximity without establishing aggregate burden or endo-lysosomal localization.
row.Finding quote: When comparing the interactions between corresponding combinations of the apoE termini, intermolecular FRET was higher for E4 and lower for E2, with E3 adopting intermediate FRET levels.

row.Finding quote: When comparing the interactions between corresponding combinations of the apoE termini, intermolecular FRET was higher for E4 and lower for E2, with E3 adopting intermediate FRET levels.

row.Finding description: Capsaicin decreased lysosomal cholesterol accumulation in ApoE4-plus-PHF BV2 microglia, imaged in 8–18 fields from three biological replicates; this is a pharmacological rescue with ApoE4 exposure fixed.
